title: Convert a bunch of gconstpointers to void pointers
description:
As README.developer says:

"Avoid GLib synonyms like gchar and gint and especially don't use
gpointer and gconstpointer, unless you are writing GLib callbacks and
trying to match their signature exactly. These just obscure the code and
gconstpointer in particular is just semantically weird and poor style."

We didn't convert gconstpointers in convert-glib-types.py until
5f807da9ba, so make another pass and do so on everything except our
dissector code. Convert some gpointers as well.

Ping #19116

notes.body:
added 1 commit
  • 0600b687 - Convert a bunch of gconstpointers to const void pointers
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/16290/diffs?diff_id=1056059739&start_sha=06ec0e7e26f6548fde13812545568967581fb2d3)
Maybe a `gboolean`-to-`bool` conversion to be done here?
It's used as a `GEqualFunc` in [a g_hash_table_new_full](https://docs.gtk.org/glib/type_func.HashTable.new_full.html) call, so it has to be a `gboolean`.

So the difference is that `gpointer` and `gconstpointer` are just typedef syntactic sugar, and replacing them with the underlying type isn't a problem, but `gboolean` is a different type from `_Bool`, so you can't just change it unless you can change places where the functions are used?

Right.

`gpointer` and `gconstpointer` might somehow be useful in cases where generated code wants to create functions or variables using type names, and it's important to ohave only a single token, but they're syntactic sugar.

`gboolean` is a typedef int, and has different properties than `_Bool`, e.g. the effect of shifting it or doing a bit operation, tests other than strict boolean comparisons, use in bit fields (where a one bit `gboolean` effectively has values -1 and 0 on many compilers), it's at least 4 bytes wide unlike `_Bool`, etc. So in function pointers and pointers in general can't be freely substituted.

In C++, type mangling means that it can be an API or ABI break to switch, if some platforms used ` long` while others used `long long` for `gint64` (and similar with `int` and `long` and `gint32`, but luckily we don't care about that as much between versions.)
